utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution had a preliminary to raise. We do that only at 20 minutes to 10.00 because there were technical difficulties which delayed the start of the proceedings. Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll be as brief as possible. I thought it best just to raise this now in case -- outside the presence of the witness. Your Honour on Monday at the conclusion of the examination-in-chief of this witness correctly pointed out that one of the clarifications on the exhibit currently marked for identification as P750 modified a quotation contained in a question, a quotation from a document contained in a question. The document in question is 65 ter 10181 which is an associated exhibit to the statement. We've gone back and looked at the original transcript from that previous trial in both the English and the French, and the document which was quoted, and you were correct, Your Honour, in pointing out that it is actually even a more complicated issue than just the fact it that it was a question. So the Prosecution makes the following proposition which I spoke to Mr. Lukic about and which I understand he has no objection to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are speaking --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at a high speed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sorry. To which I understand Mr. Lukic has no objection, and that would be to strike the question which was the subject of this clarification from the statement as well as the answer which followed it. And then I would seek leave from Your Honours to -- technically I think it would be to re-open the direct to pose the question from the document to the witness and have him answer it in live testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Lukic agrees with that, and he apparently does, then the Chamber has no problem. Then we briefly go into closed session in order to allow the witness to come in.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning, Witness RM055. I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning once again. I presume you have your statement before you in French?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 32 of the French version, the last paragraph. It is P749. In the English, page 24, the third paragraph; in the B/C/S, page 44, the third paragraph. In that part of your statement, you commented upon a document, 10402. It was a letter of protest sent by --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- Chief of Staff, Brigadier-General Nicolai on the 1st of July, which is your letter of the 30th of June. I will not refer to it, the document itself, since we are in open session. As you see, you say that it was a list of incidents drawn up by your command for Bosnia and Herzegovina. In it, there are 15 incidents which occurred in the Sector Sarajevo zone of responsibility. First of all, you say that cannon fire was opened at UN convoys which were transporting supplies to the city. My question is this: Is it true, is it correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt -- my microphone is on. I'm sorry to interrupt, but I think counsel referred to the wrong 65 ter number for that document. I believe he's referring to 11196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem with your microphone. I see the light is on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you -- does this one work?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the interpreters can hear you, then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I believe the document that counsel was referencing on page 24 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it from the translation that the interpreters have no difficulties. I'm, at this moment, on the English channel. Could that be confirmed by the English interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, it can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But apparently madam transcriber has problems in hearing you, and we have as well. Could.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I believe it's 11196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that out of the reach of the microphones, the parties are resolving the matter. At the same time, Ms. Hochhauser, could you say a few words to see whether it's now okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Hello. Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's only one word. Let me see. Madam transcriber? Everything is okay. We can proceed. Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. I just wanted to point out that I believe the 65 ter number that counsel referred to for the document containing the list is RM11196, not the -- not the 65 ter number that he cited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This being corrected, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The ERN number I have is ZA016157, and that's the document discussed in the paragraph I'm referring to, and I think that the number I quoted was the number I want to discuss. All the chart is the number my learned friend mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is yours an ERN number or is it a 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I mentioned 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said ERN.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I said ERN. It's ZA016157. It's ERN. And I have it as 65 ter 01402.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Well, it's not on our screen anyhow. You didn't want to show it. So let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I read the part of the statement I wanted to read. I just want to ask the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if the confusion continues, then we should have it on our screen and we should look at it, although in -- not to be shown to the public. But let's proceed first and see whether there's any confusion or misunderstanding among the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that UN convoys moved outside the routes that had been pre-arranged with the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it also correct that they moved about in improperly marked trucks? They were not marked properly.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. All these trucks were trucks that were either military trucks or trucks that had been rented by the UN HR.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The trucks, which moved along unscheduled routes, went either early, at dawn, or at dusk, just before the night fell.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was correct at the beginning of the operation. Later on, the trucks went at different times of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say that later on the trucks went at different times of day, was it then that fire was opened on such convoys?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were the same routes used by military trucks, transporting members of the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That route was improved and enlarged by the French military engineering soldiers was used during the day by the civilian and military means of the UN, and at night besides civilians and also Bosnian military -- well, Bosnian Muslims, I meant to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Neither you nor the Army of Bosnian Muslims did notify the Serbs or the Serb side what was being transported on such trucks and when such convoys were to move about.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is partly true. At that time, or at this time, I would like to remind you, sir, the situation that was prevailing, I said so before, meaning yesterday, the Blue Routes were blocked, indeed, for the past few months. Grievous incidents had taken place on these Blue Routes that were created by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Within that city tensions, economic, social tensions were on the upward trend, linked to the heat that year, linked to the lack of supplies, and linked to the fact that they were closed in. Facing the impossibility in spite of the repeated demands or requests of re-establishing the freedom of movement that was guaranteed by the Bosnian Serb side on the Blue Routes, we have suggested several options, in order to re-establish this freedom of movement. The option that was selected in June was to unblock the city of Sarajevo by opening up a passage without looking --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please stop. I apologise. My question had to do with fire opened at such convoys which were moved along the routes that were not approved by the Serbs. I'm not asking about the Blue Routes or the city and the social situation on nutrition, et cetera. Let us stay focussed, please, and kindly try and answer my questions. I apologise, but I have time-limits, and we all need to invest an effort into putting the right questions and receiving appropriate answers. If there are any topics that are left open, the Prosecution will have an opportunity to discuss it with you.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do understand, so I will answer your question thus. These convoys were not announced to the Bosnian Serb side. On the other hand, each time that the fire was opened from the Ilidza Brigade on these convoys, there was a reaction with fire by the United Nations units. When this fire was an artillery fire, myself would tell my counterparts of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of such fire that would be opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You talked about the road being expanded, made wider. The French Battalion actually created the road and fixed it in such a way that trucks could move along it, whether -- whereas, before that, it had predominantly been a footpath; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The work that was undertaken enabled the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina to use that route to dispatch trucks, transporting different kinds of goods to Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correction: We facilitated transport through this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did UNPROFOR check what kind of goods were being transported on the trucks of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The UNPROFOR did not check the civilian trucks or any other trucks using this route by night.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The road ended at the tunnel, or, rather, the routes of the Army of BH trucks ended at the entrance to the tunnel in the settlement of Butmir; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This itinerary was close to the entrance of the tunnel and continued to the western entry point of the airport area controlled by the UN forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, the route was actually the backbone of all supply for the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to remind you what I said earlier on. The mode of action consisted in deblocking the city of Sarajevo without trying to have confrontation with the Bosnian Serb army but by retaliating, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The thrust of my question went more in the direction of UNPROFOR knowing that the route was being used to supply the BH Army with ammunition and weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: UNPROFOR knew that this run was used by the army, by the Bosnian Muslims, and this seemed in compliance with the principle of impartiality between both parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know if I understood your answer properly. Are you trying to say that the Serb side agreed to the route created by the French Battalion to be used to supply the Bosnian Muslim army in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This route had been built by the French Battalions and not the Serbs. The Bosnian Serb party, of course, disagreed, because their aim was to block as tightly as possible the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you a question pertaining to military doctrine. Is it justified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, we move to a different subject at this moment, or are we still -- because I'd like to clarify the issue which created so much confusion at the beginning of this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please do so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. 65 ter 11196, that was the number referred to by Ms. Hochhauser, is, indeed, a letter of protest dated the 8th of June in two languages. A list is attached which, by the way, does not -- is not mentioned in the letter. It's a list of incidents. Therefore, it's a bit confusing what the list exactly has to do with the letter. Now, the English version also contains the B/C/S version of the letter. In e-court the B/C/S translation covers only the list and not the B/C/S version of the letter, which, again, is found in the English version. 65 ter 1402 is a letter written by a woman which appears only in B/C/S and there's no English translation in e-court, as far as I could see. Therefore, it seems that what you are quoting off or at least what you were referring to, Mr. Lukic, is, indeed, 65 ter 11196.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I actually -- I came to a different conclusion about what the confusion was. I think that the ERN number as it's listed in the statement actually includes two 65 ter numbers and that's 11196 and 10402. So I think perhaps the record didn't catch the whole of the 65 ter -- second 65 ter that I had listed. I think I can -- the 10402 contains the list. I'm sorry. 11196 contains the list and 10402 contains the letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then there was, therefore, another confusion about whether it was 10402 or whether it was 01402. That was confused as well. I think everything has been straightened out now on the record. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although perhaps I ask one thing. Ms. Hochhauser, in 65 ter 11196, the letter and the list are combined. Now, the letter dates of the 8th of June, 1995. However, the list describes events happening between the 30th of June and the 3rd of July, 1995, which requires, for the person writing that letter, certain capacities which I do not have. That is, what will happen in the month to come. They are apparently with the same fax header so they certainly would have been sent at one point in time together to whomever, but I'm really surprised by -- to see attached to a letter of the 8th of June, 1995, to see what happened between the 30th of June and the 3rd of July of that same year.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that the cover letter, which is the first page of 10402, lists both of these letters separately. In any event, what I would endeavour to do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Hochhauser, then have a look at it and tell me, as a matter of fact, I do not see any list referred to at all. So if you would then please bear with me and explain to me where on D11196 reference is made to the list, then I would be happy.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I might suggest if it's amenable to the Court is that I take look at the hard copies of these -- both documents, that can I look at them together and revert -- come back to you with an answer at the end of this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser, they're not in evidence. Hard copies are at this moment not available to the Chamber. The only thing we have is the material in e-court, and therefore since you started saying what you believed was in 10402, that is, a reference to two lists, then I wonder whether your hard copy appears under the same 65 ter number, and, as you know, hard copies usually or do not always give a clear indication as to the number under which they are uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- I'm -- I'm sorry if I'm being confusing. I'm referring to the first page of 10402 as uploaded in e-court, which is a fax cover sheet, which lists what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Could you please have it in e-court. What I have in e-court for 65 ter 11196 is a three-page document. The first page, although having fax headers, and -- two fax headers even, so they must have been copied, one with page 04, the other one with page 13, but it is an UNPROFOR document, it is a letter, to the left in English, to the right in B/C/S, sent by Major-General Gobillard to Major-General D. Milosevic. That's the first page. The second page is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, should we go to private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that the Muslim forces had 128-millimetre rocket-launchers with a range of 10 kilometres? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Bosnian Muslim forces within Sarajevo had a few pieces. We were monitoring a few of them that were concealed in road tunnels at the east exit of Sarajevo. These pieces never fired during my presence from May to October, except one time after the cease-fire which brought us to an operation in order to get these pieces back. That was the only time that I saw a mortar of 120 fire, and we heard yesterday that a depot was in a unused factory about 400 to 500 metres from the PTT building. These pieces had never gone out of that depot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, time for a break. We first turn into closed session so that the witness can leave the courtroom. And we'll be back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need in e-court document 65 ter number 18010, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you will see, sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to state something about the document for the transcript. It is a Sector Sarajevo UNPROFOR unit of the 9th of July, 1995, by Captain Guegan. This document should not be broadcast outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see who it was sent to. You do recognise that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next, in the B/C/S, we need page 3, as well as page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph, we see the following: "... Captain Novak proposes to Mr. Guegan that we announce in advance the arrival of our convoys. He said that white vehicles had been used by the BH Army and that, for instance, two white vehicles that the Serbs shot at and destroyed on the logistics run a few months ago did not provoke a strong protest." Do you recall now that UNPROFOR was informed that the SRK was asking for UNPROFOR convoys to be announced so that fire would not be opened?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And what is the question that you're asking, if I may?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall now that UNPROFOR was informed of the request by Sarajevo-Romanija Corps to have all convoys announced so that no fire would be opened upon them?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that in the report that is mentioned, the captain, Captain Novak, said that, according to him, vehicles, Bosnian vehicles, were attacked. I do not remember that there was this type of a request in this report. And I'm looking at the French version. Well, my mistake, sorry. Sorry. I'm really sorry. Indeed, the request was put through by Captain Novak during this meeting. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A moment ago, you told us that Muslim forces had 128 portable rocket-launchers and that you found such pieces in the eastern tunnel leading to Pale; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did UNPROFOR seize those weapons? Did they open fire at UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the incident occurred after the cease-fire. A local initiative made that this piece had been withdrawn from its depot, put in a battery on the road, and one or two projectiles were fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was UNPROFOR also aware of the fact that the Muslim forces in Sarajevo had 107-millimetre rocket-launchers, produced in Iran, if I'm not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall this type of weapon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that when a rocket-launcher is being fired it has a direct trajectory which cannot be picked up by any radar devices?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of course, a rocket has a straight trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Sarajevo, were you told that the French ambassador protested with President Izetbegovic because the forces of the Muslim army killed a French soldier? The protest and the killing took place in April 1995.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, I was not in Sarajevo at that time, and I have no knowledge of this protest. I'm discovering it today. In any case, I had no hierarchical link with the ambassador of France. We merely were trying to help an isolated fellow citizen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like us to focus now, again, on the tunnel. You said a few moments ago that the road constructed by the French passed by the tunnel; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there ever any attempts to prevent the passage of military equipment through the tunnel or was there no reaction whatsoever? Or was it even approved by the French Battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Approved of by the French Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time I was on duty in Sarajevo, we did not try to stop the passage of equipment through that tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were in Sarajevo, or before your arrival, did you have occasion to read an agreement by which the Serbs handed over the airport to UNPROFOR? And do you know what kind of obligation was there on UNPROFOR in the running of the airport?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about it, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You do know, then, that UNPROFOR was supposed to prevent any crossing over of soldiers or passing of military equipment and weapons and vehicles?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir. If you give me some more time, maybe I could elaborate on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tunnel characteristics did not allow for heavy equipment passage. The transitional capacity of this tunnel was very limited, even if it had been used 24/7. Besides, given the conditions arising from the blockade of Sarajevo, we considered that some balance had been stricken in the spirit of impartiality as I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you were aware of the characteristics of the tunnel. Did you visit it personally, or did you receive reports about it? What were you told about the width and height of the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went through the tunnel myself. I was invited to do so, but I refused. And from the reports that I received, the width and height characteristics of the tunnel made it that it was a small-size tunnel, and this was later checked after the cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any UNPROFOR members took part in the construction of the tunnel or in the attempts to make it wider?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us focus next on UNPROFOR movements. Let me ask you this: You said that UNPROFOR was not able to visit hospitals. Is it also correct that UNPROFOR had no access to certain parts of town because the Muslim side, the Muslim forces, would not allow it?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should be nuanced. Our teams were not totally free to access any hospital at any time. Likewise, some inspections were not facilitated by the Bosnian Muslim side in some parts, among others, around Mount Hum. The same obstacles had been present before my arrival and continued after that in the Bosnian Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. Let me ask you this next: We have some UNPROFOR documents, referring to a Muslim offensive. I believe we will agree, as it tallies with what you had stated, that Muslim offensives with certain interruptions lasted from the moment of your arrival until the Serb positions were bombed. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not entirely. The first Bosnian Muslim Corps attacks happened between the 15th of May and the 28th or 29th of May. There was an interruption caused by the failure of the operations and the reaction of the other side and the fact that the units were exhausted. After that we witnessed, again, limited attacks at the end of the month; among others, around the 28th and 29th of June, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there an offensive which was stopped on the 8th or 9th of June and it followed the first one, which started on the 28th or 29th of May? If you recall; if not, let us move on.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If memory serves, I would say that your dates are approximately correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us be more specific now. The offences -- offensives were launched from all parts of town. Is it correct that in the north there was an offensive aimed at the Cemerska heights?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that place, Cemerska heights. The main axis of the attack were, let me remind you, in the south, towards Lukavica, and in the west, towards Ilidza. As for the dates, June the 8th and 9th, I can confirm now that these are the dates where the attacks re -- were relaunched.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will try to jog your memory, if I may. In your statement, the French version, page 40, third paragraph; in the English, page 29, the last paragraph; and, in the B/C/S, page 55, the first and second paragraphs. This is what is stated: "Thank." And then the next paragraph says: "Yes, literally, the last Friday and Saturday, the 15th and 16th of June, Bosnian troops attacked Serb positions all along the confrontation line, attacking out of the city and into it from the south, west, and north. Can you confirm that you also knew this, that they were launching attacks both out of the city and from the south, west, and north?" Your answer was: "Yes. This is consistent with our observations. I cannot mention that these dates mentioned the 15th and 16th of June are the right ones, mentioned by David Harland. The combat operations continued over a period of one month. Our monitoring of this was to see and realise that Bosnian troops were deployed towards the south, the south-west of the city, that they were basically in that part of the city." Do you accept this part of your statement? Kindly repeat your answer. It was not picked up by the transcript.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat what I said at the time and what I told you earlier on. The main axis were on the south and in the east --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In the west, correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, is it also correct that such attacks took place in the city itself; for example, in the direction of the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the area of the Jewish cemetery towards Lukavica, that's the southern part of the front that I've been talking about for quite sometime now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But not out of the city but in the city itself; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the confrontation line, of course, which was at the height of the Jewish cemetery towards the Bosnian Serb lines and towards the general direction of Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you something else about your statement. In the French, it is 37; in the English, 27, the very bottom; and in the Serbian, in the B/C/S, it is page 50, under the Roman numeral VII. There you refer to a statement. There is an ERN number in the statement itself --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see document 10184, to that end. I would kindly ask that it is not broadcast outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There, we see, on the first page, that Mr. Harland informed Philip Corwin and also included Mr. Akashi, under info. In the third paragraph it reads: I would like to inform you that the acting sector commander, and then we have the name, believes that the BH Army was deploying its mortars around the PTT building so that it could draw fire to it where close to it, close to the place which is fought over in order to control the western part of Sarajevo, and that is it. Do you recall that the BH Army placed its mortars around the PTT building, that is to say, the headquarters of UNPROFOR, and that it used those mortars in combat?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interject, but when I read from the document, as I see it on the screen, it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any dispute about the way in which a reference is made to the document, you should literally read the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: The -- the portion that I would point to is the second sentence of the third paragraph where it says -- the transcript shows that Mr. Lukic reading that the Bosnian army is placing its mortars around the PTT building. The document as I read it says it is not placing its mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not in such a way, isn't?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not in such a way, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... draw fire onto the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's exactly the reason why I asked for a literal quote then and not -- if you are unhappy with it, then Mr. Lukic, as I said in the beginning, should literally quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's what is he now going to do, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. But we have to go a private session for a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to deal with the time just before the bombing of the Serb positions. I think that I know the answer, but I do have to ask you. In your view, did the Serbs have the right to take weapons from the Weapons Collection Points if they were attacked by the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know my answer so I will state it again. The text of the protocol that was presented by the Bosnian Serb side during the signing of the said agreement anticipated the possibility of taking up the weapons if the UNPROFOR was not able to keep attacks from happening against the Serb side. As much as I know, this protocol was not approved by the UN authorities. So that was my first point. Second point that I've already stated was that the nature, the power of attacks that were given by the 1st Bosnian Muslim Corps reacting to the situation that they were presented with, did not justify from a technical and professional point of view -- did not justify, from a technical and professional point of view, did not justify the taking back of additional weapons. Enough heavy weapon of artillery were deployed around Sarajevo so as to able to react when faced with these attacks from the Bosnian Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that Mr. Akashi, together with Mr. Karadzic, signed that protocol.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have 1D557 on our screens. We need the third page. Can we please have page 3. These are the paragraphs of the agreement. We see on page 3 that this document was signed by Mr. Akashi and Mr. Karadzic. So can we now please have page 4 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see in paragraphs 1 and 4 precisely what you said to us just now. If UNPROFOR withdraws for any reason or if they cannot stop the attacks of the Muslim army, the Serbs do have the right to take these weapons. You said to us just a moment ago that you believe that the attacks of the Muslim army were not strong enough to justify the taking of these weapons. However, in paragraph 4 of this protocol, it says, and I'm going to read it out in English so that you can get the right interpretation: "[In English] Neither the Serb nor the Muslim side is permitted to engage in military activities of any description, and this includes consolidation of trenches or their forward movement and similar activities ..." [Interpretation] Would you agree with me that this protocol - and we'll go back to the issue of whether it is valid or not - that this protocol does not allow any kind of military activity whatsoever. This protocol does not refer to any kind of stronger or weaker military activity. Any kind of military activity is ruled out. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the document that we have on the screen, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that the UN authorities - we heard that that just now - did not accept this protocol that was signed by Mr. Akashi. Would you please be so kind as to tell us whether the UNPROFOR authorities ever informed the Serb side or the Muslim side - or perhaps the Croat side - about that, that they did not accept the protocol signed by Mr. Akashi?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You personally did not receive any information to that effect? Namely, that the UN authorities informed anyone of the three warring parties in Bosnia-Herzegovina about this protocol not being valid.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall repeat, that, at the time, I only knew the -- the official text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree that without meeting the prerequisites referred to in paragraphs 1 and 4 of this agreement, it is not possible to implement the agreement on weapons collection?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand your question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably I didn't put the question probably so I'll try to put it in more understandable terms. A prerequisite for the collection of Serb weapons at points that are controlled by UNPROFOR, was a prerequisite for that, that there should be no fighting and that Muslims should not carry out any offensive actions. Can you answer that?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that the weapons -- that some weapons had been collected previously on these collecting points, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I am not in a position to provide answers from where I stand today. As for weapons collecting points, was there a cessation of hostilities? Because weapons could not be collected while fighting was going on; right?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the agreement was signed and implemented, there was a quiet period in 1994, before I came to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I would like to ask the witness for a certain clarification. On page 32, the witness, in line 15 and 16 said: I shall repeat that at the time I only knew the official text. I understand that the text we just saw on the screen was not accepted by UN authorities. To which official text are you referring in your answer? What agreement do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, it was the agreement that organised the collecting points for weapons. And I do not remember, I do not remember, I do not recall this additional page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "this additional page"? You mean this page we have on the screen now, signed by Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Akashi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's this page that I personally do not remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And, again, I would like to understand that. Which agreement was, in your view, valid and accepted by the UN officials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The weapons were collected on collection points in the safe area, and they were under the control then of -- of UNPROFOR units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That doesn't answer my question. Which agreement do you mean? Agreement which led the -- agreement about establishment of these weapons collection points? Which agreement do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. The agreement in January 1994 on the setting up of the collection point in the safe area. That's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps, Mr. Lukic, I'm also a bit confused. If I were able to understand your line of questioning, what you present is a message which was sent in August 1994 by Mr. Akashi to Mr. Annan. That's the outgoing code cable. What we see is that attached to it is a signed document of February 1994, if I am -- so that's from many months before. Then you say that is signed, and the suggestion is that the protocol, which is not signed, and which is not referred to in any way in the February 1994 document, although it is mentioned in the code cable, would apply, if I understand you well, on the basis of the signature under the February 1994 document. But I may have missed something, but -- but that is what I got from the questions you've put to the witness and the witness has not always been very precise in referring to agreements. So we have a January agreement, which is not in this document; we have a February agreement signed by Karadzic and Akashi; we have a code cable in August, to which this protocol is attached, without any reference to agreement reached. Just it's mentioned. It's referred to. It's unsigned. So I'm -- I'm trying to understand exactly what was applicable agreement at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand the same thing, Your Honour, but obviously we got this document from the Prosecution and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But there's a strong suggestion in your line of questioning that the signature under the February document would -- in one way or another, would justify an assumption that the protocol which is here mentioned in the August 1994 code cable, that that would be agreed among the parties -- or would apply apart from, again, the context -- the content of the document, as far as consequences are concerned. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please take a look at 65 ter number 10248.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a report from a meeting with the Army of Republika Srpska. Co-ordination of heavy weapons withdrawal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is under seal, the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a document dated the 18th of September, 1995. And it was drafted after the bombing of Serb positions; is that right? The air-strikes started on the 30th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we stay on page 1 in English. And can we have page 2 in B/C/S, number 16 (b).

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "In case of any major provocations or attacks by the BiH from the city centre or from outside, all weapons are to be quickly redeployed, in less than 24 hours, and heavy shelling of BiH positions is to be expected. They want this warning to be acknowledged." Do you remember that after the bombing, the Serbs understood the withdrawal or collection of weapons as follows: If they are attacked, they have the right to use those weapons. So these are the same rights that are envisaged by the protocol that we were looking at a moment ago. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which point exactly of the protocol you're referring to at this moment, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraphs 1 and 4. Primarily 1. Because 4 is even more strict, saying, No military activity whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And your question would be, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does the gentleman remember that the Serbs, even after the bombing, stated that they had the right to use their heavy weapons that they had previously handed over if they are attacked by the Muslims, that is to say, for the purpose of self-defence which, in our view, is only logical.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I remember very well this statement made by Colonel Lugonja, and we had very good relations. And he clearly stated that they would resume the collection of weapons if they were attacked. I can confirm that. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again, we are now talking about apparently what is put down in the protocol as a right reserved by the Bosnian Serbs and which apparently is then repeated as a claim, because it's on the basis of the language, it's not more or less than that, they stress the following points, as it reads. There's nothing about an agreement. It -- it all -- the whole discussion, the whole questioning, is about whether it applies. Shall we focus on that first before we start interpreting? And if you say, That's unclear to me, you put the question to the witness whether the Bosnian Serbs were ever informed that it was withdrawn or would not apply. Now that question becomes relevant if there, first of all, is evidence that there is an agreement or that there is a reason to assume that it would apply. And that was the gist of my previous comments, that, on the basis of these documents, it seems -- at least we have difficulties in finding a solid basis for such an assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I was not the creator of these documents so we will probably have to explore this matter in the future with other witnesses as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm certainly not -- but, I think, as a matter of fact, in preparing for the questions that you have put to the witness that you should have explored it already. But let's stay away from that. Certainly if the question is, Have you given notice that it does not apply or does not apply anymore, then the previous question should be, On what basis would one accept that it did apply up till such a withdrawal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you heard His Honour. Can you assist us in what he would like to know? Do you know whether the protocol was applied, implemented, before your arrival or after your departure?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before my arrival, well, I can't tell you anything, and I'm sure that you will understand that. After my arrival, I noticed that the weapons had been withdrawn from the WCPs, not after the Bosnian Muslim attacks, but when NATO started its air-strikes. When the weapons were withdrawn after the cease-fire, and I said it already, Mr. Lugonja recalled that point and insisted on the fact that this point should be drawn to the attention of all parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Could I just ask that for clarification when we're referring to protocols, that we say which protocol it is that we're referring to, whether it's the protocol that's labelled that the -- the back of the Defence exhibit that's labelled "Protocol of Understanding Between the Civilian and Military Representatives of the Republika Srpska and UNPROFOR," that's the unsigned part of the -- the Defence document or some other protocol? Because I think there seems to be some completion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we called the document 1D557 and that's exactly the protocol we are addressing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the fourth and the fifth page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's one document. That's how we received it from the Prosecution. And, actually, now we'd like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is -- it is a document that we provided and as such I don't have any objection to its as admission based on its authenticity or derivation. Obviously I -- I -- I'm not acceding to the idea that this last protocol is a signed document that was -- that was ever put into force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D557 receives number D135, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D135 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Judge. I was just handed a note that says that it's already in evidence as D112. I don't know if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I have never tendered it. Is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Not in e-court under this number, this 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on and I hope we will clarify it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We leave it for the time as it is before we vacate that number, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, at the same time, Mr. Lukic, how much time would you still need? You said one hour and ten minutes. I think we're now at approximately one hour and 3 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll need ten, 15 minutes. Ten to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten to 15 minutes. That would be too much, I take it, for -- using before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you want us to take the break now, Your Honour, and maybe I can condense my remaining --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would try to condense it to ten minutes, and it also gives an opportunity to all parties to get their administration in proper order. The Chamber will try to do the same. We're -- we turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for having this in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll not reconsider the status of this portion of the transcript, Mr. Lukic. It's ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Now you'll finish in ten minutes, I take it, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hopefully yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, we are near the end. Let us gather some last portions of strength and finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 1D488. To have it clear on the record it was shown today as 1D557.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record, this is Exhibit D112.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the transcript, it's P112. It should be D112.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The point is made, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I hope it's finally clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, we go back to this document of the 16th of August, 1994, sent by Mr. Akashi to Mr. Annan. We need page 2 of the document, paragraph number 3. I'll read it out so that we are familiar with the topic itself. [In English] I quote: "The protocol to the Sarajevo WCP Agreement of 14 February 1994 (attached) recognises the BSA's legitimate right of self-defence. If the BSA comes under more pressure from the B and H, their demand to have access to their weapons could become a more pressing reality, under the protocol referred to above. There are several scenarios that could prevail, and the staff at BH Command and UNPROFOR HQ are examining these." [Interpretation] Sir, were you ever informed, in totality, of the protocol discussed herein by Mr. Akashi?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do remember this document that is here. The two pages are rather clear in my memory. This is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you seem to recall a protocol, particularly the one mentioned in this letter?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in reality, no. Would my memory not serve? Well, I'm sorry. I couldn't give you a more specific answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it clear to you then that there was a protocol, and you say you saw these two pages. There was a protocol recognising the right of the Army of Bosnian Serbs to take those weapons which had been assembled at the WCPs, or Weapons Collection Points?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you say it grants the right or -- could you please be very precise and put the relevant portion of the protocol on the screen or read it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I read the protocol to the witness and he said that he does not remember that protocol but that's the protocol we saw before. It's the protocol attached to this letter mentioned in this point 3 of Mr. Akashi's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are you referring to recognising the right of the Army of the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In this protocol?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this protocol, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see then. Is it in 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In 1, it reads, and perhaps we could have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's page 4 of the document: "The BSA reserves the right to redeploy its weapons and increase troop levels, if ..." that is not exactly the same as what you put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's why I asked the witness whether he remembers any other protocol.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Let me see ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There must be a protocol. Either this one or another one. We have this one attached to the letter. If there is another one, we would be happy to see the other one as well. But for now we have to work with this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the only thing I'm -- we can work with this one. You characterised the document by saying, There was a protocol recognising the right of the army of the Bosnian Serbs to take those weapons. What I'm drawing your attention, this protocol doesn't say the Bosnian Serbs have the right but the Bosnian Serbs reserve the right, which is not the same. To redeploy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if I reserve a right, it first has to be established that I have that right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in case the right was mentioned before. If the -- [Overlapping speakers] ... withdraws --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- or Muslim must -- in case of Muslim attack. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They reserve the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not -- perhaps it's a matter more of argument more --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Indiscernible], yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whether the language used here to reserve a right is the same as that a right is acknowledged by whomever who would be a party to this protocol, whether that would be the UN, whether that would be the Muslim --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- forces. But to reserve a right is a claim to a right, a right acknowledged is a right accepted. I wanted -- the only thing I wanted to do is to make a clear linguistic distinction between acknowledge a right and to reserve a right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I don't remember receiving an answer. Were you able to see another protocol attached to this letter, or did you see any other protocols in general? Dealing with this topic.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I am concerned, I remember clearly the text that I saw earlier. I do not recall, I didn't see in my memory or I do not recall, having seen this protocol nor other protocols at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Concerning this matter, I wanted to ask you this: It was ordered that Serb positions be bombed. The reason for the order on bombardment which began on the 30th of August, 1995 was what, if you could tell us?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I just wonder whether if this is an area where we might go into private session, if the witness thinks it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Out of cautious --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A brief topic. The RRF, Rapid Reaction Force, was part of UNPROFOR, was it not?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Rapid Reaction Force was under the command of the Bosnia-Herzegovina command and was the second echelon of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The command was headed by General Smith; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the Serb positions were bombed not only in Sarajevo and its environs but throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Immediately prior to Serb positions in Bosnia-Herzegovina being bombed, there was an exodus of Serbs from Croatia, from the -- between the 4th and 7th of August, 1995. You were informed about that, were you not?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was, indeed, informed of the fighting in the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fighting spilled over from Croatia into the neighbouring parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Were you informed of that as well?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not follow very specifically the information concerning this sector, which was not under our responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will be jumping from one topic to another since I'm trying to close. You had observers who had been trained especially to guide planes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct. These are teams that was specialised for guiding aeroplanes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll briefly go back to the tunnel. Please focus and stay with me, especially the side of the tunnel running underneath the Sarajevo airport runway. Were you informed that, after some time, there were rails placed in the tunnel and wagons were used to carry goods. Were you informed about that?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I learned at the time that small wagons on very narrow rails that were pushed manually were being used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this: Did you have information that, save for weapons, ammunition, food, there was also fuel that was transported through the tunnel, and that there was smuggling of illegal substances, such as drugs, that were being taken into Sarajevo. Did you have such information?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer such specific questions about drugs, et cetera. I don't know. I only remember that we could see exchanges between the mobs of both parts, on the Bosna side. I observed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, why do I ask you about that? I wanted to know whether you were informed that UNPROFOR members also took part in illegal activities, such as narcotics trade.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be very surprised, and if it were the case, these activities would be highly reprehensible and illegal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, this concludes my questions, and I thank you for answering them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could -- if we could begin in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 10996A on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And as it's coming up, this is a blow-up of a portion of Exhibit P602, which is the Sarajevo map from the Army of BiH used between 1994 and 1995. And yesterday at page 7119, beginning at line 17, you were asked a series of questions regarding the areas of responsibility of certain brigades. And, sir, you were asked: "Let me ask you generally, then, as per parts of town, do you remember the 111th Brigade was deployed around Grdonj hill and they also had Hum under their control?" And you provided an answer, and you said: "If, again, memory serves, Hum was under the responsibility of the 105th Brigade. And the 111th Brigade deployed on the eastern side of the city was supposed to control, if memory serves, between the crest, the Grdonj hill, and more to the south." So I'd like to ask, please, you testified -- you gave that testimony yesterday without the benefit of a map. So I would like to ask, please, if, first, I could draw your attention to where you see 111 on the screen on the left.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you go over one square to the right and one down from that designation. If we could zoom in on that. There's the area and I'm pointing to the area that's marked "Hum," just a little bit further over. Right there. Yep. So it's the lower and to the right. Can you locate the designation Hum? And does that refresh your recollection that hill was actually in the -- under the auspices of the 111th Brigade and not the 105th?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Apparently I wrongly mistook this -- both brigades. But as far as I remember, the 105th one was in the north and the 111th in the west, but the map says the other way around. I'm sorry, I didn't have the map in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I think you've just given us the answer to my next question would be -- which was does looking at the map, and if we could move now focus in on the designation "105 bbr." And just above it, where the area of Grdonj is marked, and I think you have just given us that answer already, but does that refresh your recollection as to the brigade that covered the area of Grdonj being the 105th?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, sir, just for clarity's sake, this is -- you were only speaking, when you testified about the brigades and their different areas of responsibility, you were testifying specifically about which brigades were responsible in those areas during your tenure in the region; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this, 10996A. Unfortunately with the exhibit that -- the large exhibit, as it's already in, if you zoom-in on it, it pixelates, so you wouldn't be able to do the same with just the exhibit that's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say therefore we need this additional copy as a separate exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10996A becomes Exhibit P753, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P753 is admitted into evidence. It's an optical improvement rather than anything else. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could please have 65 ter 10036 on the monitor. And specifically page 2 in the English but it remains 1 in the other languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, in the transcript starting at page 7128, at approximately line 1, you were asked questions about this document. And in your statement you say in the English at page 12, B/C/S page 22, and French 16, that this type of report is typical of a type of report that you would receive. Now, I'm looking at -- looking at page 2 where it begins - and if we could scroll down, please - I'm sorry. If you could focus in where it begins: "As soon as the shot was fired, Lieutenant Charette," and then it names the command post, "set up protective measures for the entire personnel, launched an investigation, and deployed a protection unit." Goes on in the next paragraph: The commanding officer arrived, names the time, became acquainted with the situation at the same time as the SP staff engaged in investigation. Three Vab wield armoured vehicles were deployed to secure the northern junction, and then there's a question mark where I think it is meant to say it's illegible, of the SP overlooking the "Sniper Alley." Then the document continues. Does this portion that I've read to you and the document itself demonstrate accurately the protective measures and investigative actions that would go into effect by UNPROFOR in response to sniping during the time that you were in Sarajevo as well?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The process was similar, with the exception that liaisons with the Bosnian Serb side did not work anymore at the time I was in Sarajevo. Did not work or worked very badly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this 65 ter number 136.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic, I see that you're still thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's 1994. Because if he tender -- if this one is accepted, I will have some questions on this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then, of course, in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I would rather not have it, since it's 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that was the -- the -- the objection that was listed by the Defence in their response to the original motion, that it was outside of the time-period. I think the questioning has just, by -- by -- the witness has just stated that this accurately still represents the process and the measures that were taken during his time-period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, of course, part of it is on the record. Would that trigger any need to put further questions to the witness if it would not be admitted? I mean, if the subject matter is of concern to you, I can imagine that you would want to put further questions to the witness, irrespective of whether we admit it or not. If you want to put such further questions, then we would admit so that we have a proper basis for understanding the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can -- ah. Exactly. Okay. Let's then admit the document and I will have [Overlapping Speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Oh, it's withdrawn. Then let me see. Yes. Madam Registrar, I don't think you have assigned a number yet. Would you please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Document 10036 becomes Exhibit P754, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P754 is admitted into evidence. And, Mr. Lukic, of course, those questions may trigger any need for further questions to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday beginning at transcript page 7144, line 24, the question was asked of you: "Is it correct that UNPROFOR was deployed in Sarajevo in such a way that on the side that was under the control of the Muslim forces, there were five battalions, namely the 2nd French Battalion, the 5th French Battalion, the 4th French Battalion, the Egyptian Battalion, and the Ukrainian battalion; whereas, on the Serb side, there was only the Russian Battalion." And you confirmed with some additional detail in your answer that this was correct. And for clarity of your -- of your written evidence, is it correct that this is because the Serb side would not accept any battalions other than the Russian Battalion on their side?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the -- whether when the battalions' deployment was ordered, whether the Serbs objected to that, but I witnessed that, practically speaking, it was impossible to deploy other battalions in the sector under Bosnian Serb control, with the exceptions of small units that were in charge of monitoring WCPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "practically speaking," is that because of some action on the part of UNPROFOR or some action on the part of the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we wished to deploy other units in the sector under SRK control, the request was rejected by this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to turn now to the topic of -- of Markale market. Yesterday in the context of -- at -- excuse me. Yesterday in the context of confirming your statement that the bombing that occurred could not have been staged, and that's at transcript 7156, line 19, you were directed to the image of a dead body folded -- that lays over a rail. In your experience in Sarajevo, was it commonplace for civilians to move or remove bodies and attempt to tend to the wounded at the scene of shellings before ambulances and officials arrived?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never a witness nor was I given any report of bodies being moved for whatever staging, if that was your question. When these unfortunate events were taking place, the first reflex was to stop the vehicle, to bring the victim in the vehicle to a hospital. There were no -- there was no reflex, if you will, to care on the spot medically this wounded person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the same videotape that you were shown yesterday, Exhibit P446, you were asked about the number 2800 that was spoken by someone who appears to be a member of the French Battalion in possession of a piece of measuring equipment from which he is reading that -- that number. On that video in the same segment that was played, and that's -- and I'm going to point to approximately 5 minutes 19 seconds to 5 minutes 29 seconds, there is other conversation in English in which it can be heard a person saying, "That is not correct. That is not correct. That's prior to the reading of the number."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not relying on this for the truth of the statement, so I don't think it's necessary, unless you see it as necessary, to re-play that segment right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean -- what do you mean by not relying it on for the truth of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't is it that you want to rely on the fact that someone said, "It's not correct," and should that then not be on the record that that is what can be heard in the video?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. We can play that section from 5 minutes 19 seconds to 5 minutes 29 seconds. While it's coming up --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question to the witness is: Do you have any personal knowledge of the particular circumstances of this measurement that we see being taken here or of how many times the measurement was taken?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can we play that same segment again to confirm that it's -- those words are being picked up for translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: "No, it's not correct. "[No interpretation]. "No, that's the angle of impact. "It's not correct. "[No interpretation]."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- perhaps we could resolve the matter another way. Would the parties agree that the words "this is not correct" are spoken in English, and that they are spoken before even the person who uses what seems to be a compass goes on his knees and starts measuring, but that those words are spoken before he really gets down on his knees and is doing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would stipulate that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you -- Witness, can you say whether you have any knowledge of the particular circumstances of this measurement we see here, or, in fact, how many times the measurement was taken?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, madam, the results, the written report was based on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- we will read all the reports and know what is in there. The question was whether you have any personal knowledge on how many times measurements of this kind were taken in relation to this crater? I take it, Ms. Hochhauser. Do you have any personal knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The measurement was done by this French adjutant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you've answered the question. The question simply was whether you have any personal knowledge about how many times it was done. Of course, you'll understand, Witness, that you're not the only witness who will talk about this event. There are reports, the totality of the evidence may be very much. Please proceed, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: May we have 10243, please, on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And as it's coming up, Witness, on a number of occasions you have referred to the French engineering reports, or report, which you relied on and -- or for which you are taking the specific information that you relaying to the Chamber. Is that report what we see on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And if we could, after a moment on the first page, just flip to the next, so he has an opportunity to confirm it. Or deny it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I shall confirm that this is, indeed, the report of the team lead, Lieutenant-Colonel Mougey on which I base myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, during the cross-examination, you were asked a series of questions about your recollection of what was said to you in reports, and except for this engineering report no specific report was put to you. Is it fair to say that if an UNPROFOR document on any of the technical aspects of -- of the Markale shelling contradicted what you've testified about your recollection of what the document said, you would rely on the document presented and not on your memory?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is perfect conformity between my observations and the document that was written up by the specialist that I mentioned earlier.
